# InspirAI — AI-Powered Design Research for Coding Agents (full context)

> `refero-design-mcp` is an MCP server for discovering, searching and extracting
> design systems from the public pages of styles.refero.design.

The underlying data belongs to Refero Design. This is an unofficial client; no
affiliation or endorsement is implied.

- Canonical URL: https://inspirai.os.darcas.app/
- Package: `@darcas/refero-design-mcp` (MIT, requires Node ≥ 22.12)
- Install: `npm install -g @darcas/refero-design-mcp`
- Repository: https://github.com/DarCas/refero-design-mcp
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@darcas/refero-design-mcp
- Short form: https://inspirai.os.darcas.app/llms.txt
- Human-readable reference: https://github.com/DarCas/refero-design-mcp#readme

`@darcas/refero-design-mcp` is an MCP server that discovers, searches and
extracts design systems from the 1,342 styles published on styles.refero.design
— palette, type scale, spacing, surfaces and do/don't guidance — so a coding
agent implements from measured evidence instead of an invented direction.

## Why it is built this way (https://inspirai.os.darcas.app/#why)

**The JSON API is not used.** `styles.refero.design/robots.txt` disallows
`/api/`, and the endpoint is gated in practice: it answers `403` to every
non-browser client and `200` to a real browser, which points at TLS
fingerprinting rather than authentication. Spoofing headers would not fix that,
and would not be the right thing to do regardless. So this server reads only
what `Allow: /` permits — the published sitemap and the public style pages —
reachable with a plain `curl` and no pretending to be anything else. Requests
are conditional, concurrency-capped, and sent with a `User-Agent` that
identifies the project:
`refero-design-mcp/<version> (+https://github.com/DarCas/refero-design-mcp;
MCP client)`.

**Coverage is reported, never implied.** A style page is a few hundred KB and
there are 1,342 of them, so the local index grows on demand. That makes "I
found no matches" ambiguous — it usually means "I looked at 30 of 1,342", not
"nothing exists". Every search states its own coverage, and
`refero_index_status` exists so the model can check before concluding that a
style is absent. The tool prints, for the repository's own cache:

```
- Published styles: 1,342
- Indexed locally: 26
- Coverage: 2%

Search and match results reflect local coverage only.
Raise `expand` on those tools to index more styles.
```

## How it works (https://inspirai.os.darcas.app/#how-it-works)

The Refero Design MCP turns one of the 1,342 published styles into a validated
record in three steps:

1. `sitemaps/styles.xml` — every style id with its `lastmod`. Small, fetched
   once.
2. `/style/{id}` — a Next.js RSC payload inside the page's HTML (~300 KB),
   fetched on demand.
3. `result.meta · result.raw · result.designSystem` — parsed, validated, cached.

The index is lazy: a search or a match only ever sees what it has indexed, so
every result states its coverage — a miss is not a verdict. The style record is
located by `styleId`: a page embeds a dozen or more related styles sharing the
same key names, so anchoring on the id prevents returning a neighbour's
palette. The RSC format is internal to Next.js and may change; every failure
surfaces as a typed error rather than a partially-filled object that looks like
a valid answer.

## Tools (https://inspirai.os.darcas.app/#tools)

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `refero_index_status` | Published styles vs. locally indexed styles |
| `refero_search_styles` | Free-text search over names, north stars, colours, fonts, URLs |
| `refero_match_style` | Ranks styles against a prose design brief |
| `refero_get_design_md` | Renders a style as `design.md`, by section |
| `refero_get_style` | Parsed design system plus measured tokens, as JSON |
| `refero_list_style_ids` | Style UUIDs from the sitemap, without reading any page |

Every tool declares all four MCP behavioural hints — `readOnlyHint: true`,
`destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: true`. None
of them mutates the origin, the cache, or anything the caller owns; all of them
can read `styles.refero.design`.

A resource, `refero://style/{id}/design.md`, is exposed for clients that prefer
resource reads over tool calls.

`refero_get_design_md` takes `sections`, and honours it: `overview · colors ·
typography · type_scale · spacing · surfaces · imagery · principles ·
components · similar · custom`. Sections with no data are dropped rather than
rendered as empty headings.

## The skill (https://inspirai.os.darcas.app/#skill)

The package also ships an Agent Skill, `refero-design-research`, that teaches a
coding agent to do evidence-based design research with the Refero Design MCP
before it implements substantial UI. The MCP answers questions about styles,
the skill decides how to ask them.

```
refero-design-skill install

refero-design-skill list                           # what is installed where
refero-design-skill install --client claude,codex  # pick clients
refero-design-skill install --project               # copy into the repository
refero-design-skill install --dry-run              # print the plan, write nothing
refero-design-skill uninstall --client claude      # remove what it installed
```

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--client <ids>` | Comma-separated ids from `skill/refero-design-research/clients.json`. An unknown id fails and lists the valid ones |
| `--scope global\|project` | Defaults to `global`. Project scope copies into the repository, because a symlink into `$HOME` breaks on another machine and in CI |
| `--global`, `--project` | Shorthands for `--scope global` and `--scope project`, which are what most other installers spell this way |
| `--all` | Every client whose detect directory already exists. Bare `install` does this |
| `--path <dir>` | Escape hatch for an unsupported client or an unusual location |
| `--dry-run` | Print the resolved plan and touch nothing |
| `--force` | Required to overwrite local modifications, and it prints the diff first |

That is the whole command. It detects the agent clients you have, writes one
shared copy under `~/.agents/skills/`, and links each client to it. Declare the
scope once: `--global --project` and `--scope project --global` both fail. **There
is no `postinstall`.** Nothing is written outside `node_modules` by installing
the package. The skill contains no Refero data: only instructions, plus a tool
reference generated from `src/`. Full text:
https://github.com/DarCas/refero-design-mcp/blob/main/skill/refero-design-research/README.md

## Evidence: performance (https://inspirai.os.darcas.app/#performance)

| Operation | Before | After | Speed-up |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `refero_search_styles` — rank 1,342 summaries | 15.5 ms | 12.6 ms | 1.2× |
| `refero_index_status` | 27.9 ms | 0.15 ms | 186× |
| `expand` scan when everything is cached | 49.0 ms | 0.10 ms | 490× |
| First call in a process | 372 ms | 70 ms | 5.3× |

**The ranking barely moved, and that is deliberate.** It was measured before
being optimised: at ~13 ms across the whole catalogue it was never the
bottleneck, so the scorer was left alone rather than tuned against a guess.

**The first call in a process is dominated by one sitemap request**, not by the
disk. That fetch is what makes coverage honest, and it is why it happens once
rather than per call.

Median of 15 runs on an Intel i9-12900F / Linux / Node 22, against a warm local
cache holding 26 of 1,342 published styles. "Before" is the previous
implementation, measured in the same session on the same machine. Your numbers
will differ; the ratio is the point, not the milliseconds.

## Configuration (https://inspirai.os.darcas.app/#configuration)

Run on demand through `npx` (no install step; `-y` suppresses the install
prompt; version pinned to the current major):

```jsonc
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "refero-design-mcp": {
        "command": ["npx", "-y", "@darcas/refero-design-mcp@1"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

With a global install, the entry can name the binary directly (only with the
global install in place, else `exit 127: refero-design-mcp: not found`):

```jsonc
"refero-design-mcp": {
  "command": ["refero-design-mcp"]
}
```

One trap, for developing this package: inside a checkout of this repository
both forms fail with `exit 127: sh: 1: refero-design-mcp: not found`, because
`npx` resolves to the local project instead of the registry. Name the package
and the binary separately:

```jsonc
"refero-design-mcp": {
  "command": ["npx", "-y", "-p", "@darcas/refero-design-mcp@1", "refero-design-mcp"]
}
```

Requires Node ≥ 22.12; npm reports `EBADENGINE` on an older runtime. Transport
is stdio by default; a second binary, `refero-design-mcp-http`, serves the same
tools over Streamable HTTP (`POST /mcp`, stateless) for clients that cannot
spawn a process — see README "Remote (Streamable HTTP)". Diagnostics go to
stderr only. The package is scoped but the binary
is not: the command is `refero-design-mcp` with no `@darcas/` prefix.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `REFERO_CACHE_DIR` | `~/.cache/refero-design-mcp` | On-disk cache location |
| `REFERO_CACHE_TTL_MS` | `604800000` | Cache freshness window (7 days) |
| `REFERO_CONCURRENCY` | `4` | Max simultaneous requests |
| `REFERO_MAX_FETCHES` | `25` | Max page fetches per tool call |
| `REFERO_MAX_RESPONSE_CHARS` | `40000` | Response budget |
| `REFERO_SITE_URL` | `https://styles.refero.design` | Origin base URL |
| `REFERO_STYLES_SITEMAP` | `{site}/sitemaps/styles.xml` | Style index |
| `REFERO_TIMEOUT_MS` | `30000` | Per-request timeout |
| `REFERO_USER_AGENT` | see `src/config.ts` | Request identification |
| `REFERO_VERBOSE` | `false` | Diagnostics to stderr |

Every setting is optional; the three worth touching first for faster research
are `REFERO_MAX_FETCHES`, `REFERO_CONCURRENCY`, `REFERO_TIMEOUT_MS`.

## Design notes (https://inspirai.os.darcas.app/#design-notes)

- **Schemas derived from real payloads, not from documentation.**
  `spacing.radius` is a per-element map (`{cards: "28px", buttons: "9999px"}`),
  not a string. `similar` is `[{business, why}]` on current styles but bare
  strings on older ones. `surfaces` is `{hex, name, level, purpose}`. A
  `typeScale` size arrives as `"17"` on one style and `17` on the next, and is
  normalised to a string at the boundary.
- **Measured and curated data are both kept.** `result.raw` holds tokens with
  usage frequency and context; `result.designSystem` holds the curated reading.
- **Truncation respects structure.** The server trims on a structural boundary
  and closes any fence it opens, so a shortened document is still valid.
- **A malformed `style_id` never costs a request.** Ids are checked against the
  UUID shape first, so a wrong id returns an error naming the tool that lists
  valid ones instead of a bare `404`.
- **Conditional requests everywhere,** so a repeat call usually costs a 304.

## FAQ (https://inspirai.os.darcas.app/#faq)

**Is this affiliated with Refero Design?** No. The underlying data belongs to
Refero Design. This is an unofficial client; no affiliation or endorsement is
implied.

**Does it write anything to my machine?** The server writes one thing: its
style cache, under `REFERO_CACHE_DIR`. Installing the package writes nothing
outside `node_modules` — there is no `postinstall`.

**Where does the cache live, and can I move it?** By default
`~/.cache/refero-design-mcp`, or `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/refero-design-mcp` when set.
`REFERO_CACHE_DIR` moves it; `REFERO_CACHE_TTL_MS` sets freshness
(`604800000`, seven days).

**Do I need an API key?** No. There is no authentication anywhere in the
package.

**Can it be used offline?** For what it has already indexed, yes: the cache is
on disk. A style not yet indexed needs a fetch, and comes back as a typed
error.

**Why does the server seem to hang when I start it by hand?** It is not
hanging. Transport is stdio, so `npm start` waits for a client on stdin.
Diagnostics go to stderr only — a quiet terminal is the healthy state.

## Facts

License MIT. 125 tests across 9 files. 6 MCP tools. 1,342 published styles.
https://inspirai.os.darcas.app/#colophon
